target_customer: Chocolate, bakery and confectionery manufacturers and food retailers that buy cocoa or cocoa butter
problem: Cocoa supply is under climate and price pressure and conventional chocolate has a large environmental footprint.
business_model: B2B ingredient sales and distribution partnerships (ChoViva cocoa-free chocolate ingredient)
product_category: Cocoa-free chocolate ingredient made from oats and sunflower seeds via fermentation

founders.name: Maximilian Marquart
education: PhD, Material Science and Mechanical Engineering
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch describes him as a material scientist and three-time entrepreneur.

founders.name: Sara Marquart
founders.background_notes: Food chemist specializing in flavor formation; sibling of Maximilian.

competitors.name: California Cultured
competitors.what: Makes chocolate without cocoa using a different (cell-based) approach

competitors.name: Voyage Foods
competitors.what: Cocoa-free chocolate alternative (named as Voyager Foods in the article)

technical_complexity.rationale: Replacing cocoa taste and cocoa butter melt behavior needed flavor chemistry, fermentation and later industrial scale production, with a PhD level founding team.

defensibility.rationale: Process know-how and a built factory give some protection, but several funded rivals pursued the same wedge and food ingredient approval and cost competition were open questions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents partnered rather than copied: Barry Callebaut agreed to distribute ChoViva in the US and a Nestle cocoa-free ingredient also comes from the company, per trade press.

market_need_then: Cocoa supply was described as endangered and pricey in the 2021 pitch, and cocoa prices later surged, which raised demand for substitutes.

branding.domain_note: Company site planet-a-foods.com; the earlier name QOA used a different domain not checked.

identity.visual_style: Consumer facing ingredient brand with product name ChoViva

branding.brand_signature: ChoViva, the retail facing ingredient brand

rebrands.why: Signals readiness for supermarket shelves, per Cocoa Post; no further reason given
Not stated in sources read; date unknown

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press covered the ChoViva rename, the Aldi UK launch and the Barry Callebaut deal; no consumer fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong trade press and retail partnerships under the ChoViva name, but QOA to Planet A Foods and Nocoa to ChoViva changes show the identity was still settling.

outcome_analysis: Planet A Foods raised a 6M USD seed in October 2021, a 15.4M USD Series A in February 2024 and a 30M USD Series B in December 2024 to expand its Czech plant from 2,000 to over 15,000 tonnes a year. Founders with food chemistry and materials PhDs, the cocoa price crisis and distribution through Barry Callebaut and retail launches such as Aldi UK explain the momentum. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff was found.
notes: Series A reported as 15.4M USD (also described as 14.2M EUR; one outlet says 14.5M USD). Total raised is reported inconsistently (23.4M vs over 43M USD). Series B sources do not state valuation. A TechCrunch headline reference to 30M USD matches the Omnes release. Coverage is partial because totals disagree.
